stem:
Navya notes that water seeps into the ground, yet wells in her area still run lower over the years. More water is pumped out, plant cover has fallen, and more ground is covered by concrete.

Why can groundwater decrease even though some water still seeps in?

options.text: Extraction and poorer seepage can remove more groundwater than seepage replaces, so the store falls.
More seepage always lowers the amount of groundwater available.
Groundwater cannot decrease while the ground looks wet on top.
Only underground lakes count as groundwater; water in soil pores does not.

teacher.key_rationale: Groundwater falls when withdrawal and reduced replenishment exceed seepage. Claiming seepage lowers stores, trusting a wet surface, or excluding pore water miss that hinge.
